cls: Nonionic, low-osmolar iodinated radiographic contrast agent
pharm: A water-soluble nonionic iodinated contrast medium (e.g., Omnipaque) whose iodine atoms attenuate X-rays in proportion to concentration, providing time-dependent radiographic contrast to visualize body structures.
quick: Individualized by procedure, concentration, body weight, and imaging technique per the labeling's dosing tables
Procedure-dependent; hydrate before and after administration
No human data; hysterosalpingography is contraindicated in pregnancy
May pump and discard breast milk for 10 hours after administration
Risk of contrast-induced acute kidney injury; minimize dose and maintain hydration
Hold metformin if hepatic impairment, alcoholism, or heart failure coexists
Alcoholism is a risk factor mandating metformin interruption around contrast
Renal function (eGFR), hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions, hemodynamics; pediatric thyroid function
summary: Iohexol (Omnipaque) is a nonionic, low-osmolar iodinated radiographic contrast agent used for intrathecal, intra-arterial, intravenous, oral, rectal, intra-articular, and body cavity imaging procedures in adults and pediatric patients. Its iodine content attenuates X-rays to opacify vessels, the CSF space, and other structures. Key safety concerns are life-threatening hypersensitivity (anaphylactoid) reactions, contrast-induced acute kidney injury (mitigated by adequate hydration and minimizing dose), cardiovascular disturbances, and - for intrathecal use - serious neurologic toxicity if the wrong iodine concentration is used (boxed warning). Iodinated contrast increases the risk of metformin-induced lactic acidosis, so metformin must be managed around the procedure in at-risk patients.
indications: Intrathecal procedures: myelography and CT myelography (lumbar, thoracic, cervical, total columnar) and CT cisternography in adults and pediatric patients aged 2 weeks and older

Intra-arterial procedures: cardiac ventriculography, aortography, selective coronary arteriography, cerebral and peripheral arteriography, intra-arterial digital subtraction angiography (IA-DSA), and pediatric pulmonary angiography
Intravenous procedures: excretory urography, CT of the head and body, peripheral venography (phlebography), and intravenous digital subtraction angiography (IV-DSA)
Oral or rectal procedures: radiographic examination of the gastrointestinal tract
Intra-articular and body cavity imaging procedures

dosage.d: Individualize concentration, volume, and rate per the labeling's procedure-specific dosing tables, accounting for age, body weight, vessel size, blood flow, pathology, and imaging technique
dosage.n: Use only concentrations/presentations recommended for each route; hydrate before and after

dosage.d: Use only the iodine concentrations and presentations specifically recommended for intrathecal procedures; OMNIPAQUE 180, 240, and 300 mg iodine/mL provide contrast for at least 30 minutes
dosage.n: BOXED WARNING - a wrong iodine concentration, even if inadvertent, can be fatal or cause severe neurologic injury

dosage.d: Concentration and volume individualized per procedure-specific tables (commonly 240-350 mg iodine/mL preparations)
dosage.n: Minimize dose and maintain hydration to reduce acute kidney injury risk

dosage.d: OMNIPAQUE Oral Solution (9 or 12 mg iodine/mL) per procedure
dosage.n: Oral solution is for oral/rectal use only - never give parenterally (risk of hemolysis from low osmolality)

admin: Use aseptic technique and only the dosage form, concentration, and presentation recommended for the specific procedure and route
Hydrate patients before and after administration of OMNIPAQUE injection
For intrathecal use, confirm the correct iodine concentration before administration (boxed warning)
Do not administer the oral solution intravenously or intra-arterially (risk of hemolysis due to low osmolality)
Always have emergency equipment and trained personnel immediately available for hypersensitivity reactions
May be warmed in a contrast media warmer up to one month, not exceeding 37 C
moa: The iodine atoms in iohexol attenuate X-rays in direct proportion to the concentration of the agent. Because the local concentration changes over time as the agent distributes and is cleared, iohexol provides time-dependent radiographic contrast that helps visualize vessels, the cerebrospinal fluid space, the urinary tract, and other body structures. As a nonionic, low-osmolar compound it is not significantly metabolized and is excreted unchanged.

absolute: Hysterosalpingography during pregnancy or suspected pregnancy
Hysterosalpingography during menstruation or when menstruation is imminent
Hysterosalpingography within 6 months after termination of pregnancy
Hysterosalpingography within 30 days after conization or curettage
Hysterosalpingography when signs of infection are present in any portion of the genital tract, including the external genitalia
Hysterosalpingography when reproductive tract neoplasia is known or suspected
relative: History of hypersensitivity reactions to iodinated contrast media
Renal impairment / risk factors for contrast-induced acute kidney injury
Patients on metformin with eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m2, hepatic impairment, alcoholism, heart failure, or receiving intra-arterial contrast
monitor: Renal function (eGFR), especially before and 48 hours after intra-arterial contrast in at-risk patients
Hemodynamic status during and after administration
Thyroid function in pediatric patients 0 to 3 years of age

preg: There are no data with iohexol use in pregnant women to inform drug-associated risks; iohexol crosses the placenta and reaches fetal tissues in small amounts. Hysterosalpingography is contraindicated in pregnant or suspected-pregnant women due to the potential risk to the fetus from an intrauterine procedure. Animal studies showed no developmental toxicity at doses up to 0.4 (rat) and 0.5 (rabbit) times the maximum recommended human intravenous dose.
lact: A lactating woman may pump and discard breast milk for 10 hours after OMNIPAQUE administration. Published literature reports limited transfer of intravenous iohexol into breast milk; the pump-and-discard interval is a precaution.
renal: Acute kidney injury, including renal failure, can occur (contrast-induced nephropathy). Minimize the dose and maintain adequate hydration before and after administration to reduce risk. In patients with renal impairment on metformin, stop metformin at or before administration and re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours afterward, reinstituting metformin only after renal function is stable.
hepatic: Hepatic impairment is a risk factor (along with alcoholism and heart failure) requiring interruption of metformin around iodinated contrast administration because of the increased risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis.

major: Metformin - iodinated contrast can increase the risk of metformin-induced lactic acidosis in renal impairment; stop metformin at or before administration in patients with eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m2, hepatic impairment, alcoholism, heart failure, or receiving intra-arterial contrast, and re-evaluate eGFR at 48 hours before restarting
moderate: Radioactive iodine (I-131, I-123) - OMNIPAQUE may interfere with thyroid uptake of radioactive iodine and reduce therapeutic/diagnostic efficacy; avoid thyroid therapy or testing for up to 6 weeks after administration
interactions.food: Hydrate patients before and after administration; oral/rectal use is procedure-dependent.
interactions.alcohol: Alcoholism is a stated risk factor that mandates interruption of metformin around iodinated contrast administration.
interactions.diagnostics: Iodinated contrast temporarily increases protein-bound iodine in blood - do not perform the protein-bound iodine test for at least 16 days after administration; T3 resin uptake and direct thyroxine assays are not affected. May interfere with thyroid radioactive iodine uptake for up to 6 weeks.

common: Pain including backache, neckache, stiffness, and neuralgia (intrathecal)
Vision abnormalities including blurred vision and photomas
serious: Contrast-induced acute kidney injury / renal failure
Thyroid dysfunction in pediatric patients 0-3 years
rare: Arachnoiditis and other neurologic effects after intrathecal use
emergency: Anaphylaxis with respiratory arrest, laryngospasm, bronchospasm, angioedema, and shock
Intrathecal toxicity from wrong concentration - convulsions, seizures, cerebral hemorrhage, coma, paralysis, acute renal failure, rhabdomyolysis, hyperthermia, brain edema, death

monitoring: Renal function (eGFR) before and, in at-risk patients, 48 hours after intra-arterial administration
Signs of hypersensitivity/anaphylactoid reactions during and after the procedure
Thyroid function in pediatric patients 0 to 3 years of age based on risk factors such as prematurity
counsel: Tell the team about any prior reaction to contrast dye, iodine, asthma, or allergies
Hypersensitivity reactions can occur during and after the procedure - report any symptoms immediately and seek care for symptoms after discharge
Drink fluids and stay well hydrated before and after the scan to protect your kidneys
If you take metformin, it may be paused around the procedure and restarted only after kidney function is confirmed stable
Report any rash that develops after the procedure
If contrast leaks at the injection site (extravasation), seek medical care if symptoms progress
pk: Peak urine concentration within the first hour after IV/intra-arterial injection
Intrathecal contrast persists at least 30 minutes; ~90% of an IV dose excreted within 24 hours
Injection: store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); warmer up to 1 month not exceeding 37 C. Oral solution: store 0-30 C, protect from light, do not freeze
pearls: Nonionic, low-osmolar agent - lower reaction rate than older ionic high-osmolar media
BOXED WARNING: use only the iodine concentrations approved for intrathecal procedures - a wrong concentration can be fatal
Hydration before and after, plus minimizing dose, is the key measure to reduce contrast-induced acute kidney injury
Hold metformin around contrast in at-risk patients and restart only after eGFR is confirmed stable at 48 hours
Oral solution must never be given parenterally (low osmolality can cause hemolysis)
Avoid thyroid radioiodine uptake studies for up to 6 weeks and the protein-bound iodine test for at least 16 days afterward
Iohexol can be removed by dialysis
missed: Not applicable - iohexol is a single-use diagnostic contrast agent administered by a clinician at the time of an imaging procedure, not a self-administered scheduled medication.
overdose: Overdosage with intra-arterial or intravenous administration can be life-threatening and chiefly affects the pulmonary and cardiovascular systems, with cyanosis, bradycardia, acidosis, pulmonary hemorrhage, convulsions, coma, and cardiac arrest. Treatment is directed at supporting all vital functions with prompt symptomatic therapy; iohexol can be dialyzed.
